groups.text: It is currently 18 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

A two-year university study suggests that banning artificial intelligence from the classroom leaves students worse off than those who use it. Thibault Schrepel, a law professor at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, split his Law of AI course into three groups to test how an AI ban, unguided use, and structured training affected performance. Students were tasked with improving provisions of the EU AI Act, graded on substance, clarity, proportionality, and innovation. The group prohibited from using ChatGPT finished last in both 2024 and 2025. These students mostly made minor wording tweaks and ran out of ideas quickly, while those with AI tools pursued more substantive legal improvements. Schrepel admitted he was wrong to assume that using AI without guidance would do more harm than good. The findings indicate a clear performance gap between students who are denied these tools and those who receive prompt engineering training.

Russian drone attacks across Ukraine killed at least six civilians and injured 43 others over the last day. Moscow launched a mass assault using 453 Shahed and Gerbera drones along with S8000 Banderol missiles, heavily targeting western regions far from the front line. One Russian drone hit a Kyiv-Warsaw train near the Polish border, prompting air threat alerts in Poland's Lublin Voivodeship. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called this "Putin's terror," stating that Russian barbarians are now at the gates of the EU and NATO. This violence persists as peace efforts stall over territorial disputes. U.S. Special Envoy Jared Kushner reported that President Vladimir Putin has demanded Ukraine cede territory in the Donbas. While Kushner noted that a deal is otherwise set up, he said Ukraine currently refuses to give up that land. Kyiv is instead calling for a ceasefire along the current front line and Western-backed security guarantees.

An attack by an unknown projectile near Hengam Island has left one crew member dead and four others injured aboard an Iranian container ship. This latest strike in the Strait of Hormuz follows reports from the UK Maritime Trade Operations and deepens a conflict where Iran continues to block traffic through the passage with threats and attacks. The U.S. military is now targeting civilian Iranian vessels under President Donald Trump’s "tanker for tanker" doctrine, a response to Iranian rocket attacks on merchant ships. This blockade of critical oil, liquefied gas, and fertilizer exports is fueling energy market instability and increasing domestic pressure on Trump ahead of November's parliamentary elections. Meanwhile, in Europe, Sweden is facing a potential political shift as the far right is poised to enter government for the first time. Opinion polls show a tight race after a comfortable center-left lead evaporated over the summer.

Enterprises are struggling to identify and manage security risks as cloud adoption accelerates. To address these vulnerabilities, a full-day virtual event is focusing on the tools and best practices needed to secure multi-cloud environments in the age of AI. This push for better infrastructure visibility comes as agentic AI introduces new insider threat models for organizations. Meanwhile, most companies remain ill-equipped to contain critical security incidents, a gap highlighted by recent reports on incident response. In a separate sphere of security, German journalist Angelique Gerai recently exposed a Russian network used to recruit disposable agents. Working under cover as a pro-Russian influencer named Katya, Gerai uncovered how the operation functioned from within Germany. These stories highlight a broad tension between the technical vulnerabilities of corporate cloud assets and the human risks posed by foreign intelligence networks.

Organizations are currently scrambling to balance security with the power of artificial intelligence as these tools integrate into enterprise operations. This tension has led to a focus on governance, identity, and the implementation of proper guardrails to manage risks. A virtual event hosted by Dark Reading explores these implications, specifically how companies can build secure AI strategies for the enterprise. In contrast to these corporate security concerns, an astronomical event is taking place this Monday. The moon will pass directly in front of Venus, creating a lunar occultation that acts as a planetary eclipse. While this phenomenon is visible in parts of Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Middle East, it cannot be seen from Brazil. However, observers in Brazil can still see the two bodies appearing very close to one another in the evening sky shortly after sunset.

Two separate ferry disasters in island nations have left hundreds of people missing after ships succumbed to bad weather. In Indonesia, the Virgo Transport 8 sank in the Java Sea on Sunday while traveling from Surabaya to Banjarmasin. Officials report that six people died and 130 remain missing, though rescuers managed to bring 107 passengers to safety. Meanwhile, in Vanuatu, the MV Matui sank Friday in heavy seas between Santo and Ambae islands. One body has been recovered and over 30 people are still missing from a vessel that carried more than 40 passengers and crew. Prime Minister Jotham Napat took charge of the search on Sunday after expressing frustration over his inability to reach senior officials. While Indonesian teams deployed helicopters and ships, Vanuatu authorities have shifted their focus toward the southeast coast where currents may have carried survivors. An investigation into negligence by the MV Matui's operator has already begun.

The CDU is reeling from a political shock in Sachsen-Anhalt, where the party plummeted nearly twenty percentage points to roughly 17 percent. This collapse coincided with a surge for the AfD, which captured almost 44 percent of the vote, narrowly missing an absolute majority of seats. The losses have fueled rumors that Chancellor Friedrich Merz could be replaced. However, CSU leader Markus Söder has dismissed these speculations, arguing that any immediate successor would face the same systemic hurdles, specifically citing a social democratic SPD that struggles with reforms. This instability comes as Germany faces another immediate test this Sunday with local elections in Niedersachsen. More than six million people are eligible to vote for nearly 29,000 seats across 2,200 municipal bodies, alongside roughly 400 direct elections for mayors and district administrators.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 16 and 20 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the Roland Ball all day, and a Silvia dance workshop at five in the evening.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
